source_scope_note.value: The supplied hardware document identifies “SIM800 Series_AT Command Manual” as related document [1], but that family-level manual was not supplied. A family-level manual is not proof that any command is supported by this particular model; the entries below are limited to commands or features explicitly named in the supplied SIM800A hardware document.

module_specific_features.feature_or_command: AT+CBAND — the document says the frequency bands can be set by this command.
AT+CBC — used to monitor VBAT voltage.
AT+IPR=x — sets a fixed baud rate and saves the configuration to non-volatile flash memory.
AT+CBATCHK=1 — can enable the over-voltage/under-voltage automatic-power-off function, which is disabled by default.
AT+CFUN=<fun> — sets minimum-functionality mode; documented values are 0, 1, and 4.
AT+CSCLK=1 and AT+CSCLK=2 — set sleep mode 1 and sleep mode 2, respectively.
AT+IFC=2,2 enables hardware flow control; AT+IFC=0,0 disables it.
AT+CMNRP=1 — configures pins 68 and 51 as UART2.
AT+CMIC, AT+CLVL, and AT+SIDET — adjust microphone input gain, output gain, and side-tone level, respectively.
AT+CSDT — enables or disables SIM-card detection.
AT+SGPIO or AT+CGPIO — set GPIO output and input voltage level.
AT+CADC — reads the auxiliary ADC voltage value.
AT + SPWM — sets PWM output period and duty cycle (spacing preserved from supplied text).
Bluetooth function can be operated by AT commands; no Bluetooth command mnemonic is named in this document.

reference_circuits.name: LDO power supply reference circuit (Figure 5)
reference_circuits.what_pdf_shows: A +5V DC-input reference using MIC29302 to VBAT, with input capacitors, an output capacitor network, and a minimum-load resistor R103; the note says R103 is required for proper regulator behavior under light load.

reference_circuits.name: DC-DC power supply reference circuit (Figure 6)
reference_circuits.what_pdf_shows: A switching-mode DC-DC reference using LM2596-ADJ, with L101, D102, capacitors, and ferrite bead FB101 in series for EMI suppression.

reference_circuits.name: VBAT input reference circuit (Figure 7)
reference_circuits.what_pdf_shows: CA is a 100uF low-ESR tantalum capacitor; CB may be a 1–10uF ceramic capacitor; 33pF and 10pF capacitors eliminate high-frequency interference; a 5.1V/500mW zener protects against voltage surge. Components are to be placed as close to VBAT pins as possible.

reference_circuits.name: PWRKEY power-on/down circuits (Figures 10 and 11)
reference_circuits.what_pdf_shows: Reference circuits for powering on/down with a transistor and with a button. The text specifies pulling PWRKEY low for more than 1 second and releasing it.

reference_circuits.name: Reset circuit (Figure 15)
reference_circuits.what_pdf_shows: The internal reset circuit is shown; RESET is internally pulled up to 2.8V and the source states that external isolation is not necessary.

reference_circuits.name: RTC backup circuits (Figures 17–19)
reference_circuits.what_pdf_shows: Three VRTC backup arrangements are shown: external large-capacitance capacitor, non-chargeable backup battery, and rechargeable backup battery.

pcb_considerations.assertion: Keep copper out of footprint area A and do not place vias in area B to avoid a short circuit between customer-board vias and module-bottom test points.
For the VBAT supply path, make PCB traces wide and short; place the power IC and bypass capacitor as close to the module as possible.
Route audio traces differentially and shield them with GND; keep audio lines away from RF cable, antenna, and VBAT, and use a good GND plane to reduce TDD noise.
For SIM layout, keep the holder away from the GSM antenna; keep SIM traces away from RF, VBAT, and high-speed lines; make traces short; and connect holder GND directly to main ground.

PCB-layout guidance: keep antenna trace from output pin to connector short, do not run RF across the whole board, keep RF away from SIM and power ICs, make VBAT and return GND short/wide, and bunch UART and USB signal lines.

Place the SIM holder near the module and far from antenna/RF cable; add ESD protection to SIM_CLK, SIM_DATA, SIM_RST, and SIM_VDD, and keep those signals away from power and high-speed-frequency signals.

antenna_requirements.assertion: There are two antenna interfaces, GSM_ANT and BT_ANT. Antenna input impedance should be 50Ω and VSWR should be less than 2. Place GSM and BT antennas as far apart as possible, with isolation greater than 30dB.
The GSM antenna must be decoupled from DC voltage, matched properly, and use a matching circuit; D101 TVS is recommended for static electricity.
For GSM matching, R101 is normally 0Ω and C101/C102 are normally not mounted; values depend on antenna debug result.
For Bluetooth matching, reserve R201/C201/C202; R201 is normally 0Ω and C201/C202 are normally not mounted; values depend on antenna debug result.

Keep the RF connector as close to GSM_ANT as possible for conducted testing, place matching circuit close to the antenna, maintain 50Ω RF-trace impedance, and keep RF traces away from high-frequency signals and strong interference sources.

protection_circuits.assertion: The VBAT input reference specifies a 5.1V/500mW zener diode to protect the module against voltage surge.
SIM_DATA should be protected against ESD with a TVS diode; the SIM-holder guidance recommends an ESD component close to the holder, such as SMF15C.
For SIM design, TVS parasitic capacitance on SIM_CLK/SIM_DATA should be less than 50pF.
For USB, maximum TVS capacitance on the data line should be less than 5pF; ESD9L5.0ST5G and ESD9M5.0ST5G are examples.
The GSM antenna matching reference recommends D101 TVS; listed recommended TVS parts are LXES03AAA1-154 (0201) and LXES15AAA1-153 (0402), both from MuRata.
The speaker and microphone reference figures visually indicate ESD elements, but the text extraction does not unambiguously identify their part numbers or complete connections.

functional.method/procedure: Pull PWRKEY low for more than 1 second and then release it; after the power-on procedure completes with a fixed baud rate set, observe the serial port.
functional.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: The module sends the “RDY” URC to indicate that it is ready to operate. The source says this URC does not appear when auto baud detect is active.

functional.method/procedure: Power off through PWRKEY or AT+CPOWD=1.
functional.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: Before power-off completes, the module sends “NORMAL POWER OFF”; STATUS is low in power-off mode and AT commands can no longer be executed.

functional.method/procedure: Pull the RESET input low, observing the reset timing diagram; Table 6 specifies VIL maximum 0.6V and pull-down time minimum 105ms.

communication.method/procedure: With auto-baud detection enabled at DCE power-on, send “A” or “a”; the document recommends sending “AT” until the DTE receives a response.
communication.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: The DTE receives “OK”, which the source states means DTE and DCE are correctly synchronized.

communication.method/procedure: After powering on, connect VBUS, USB_DP, USB_DN, and GND to a PC and install the driver successfully.
communication.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: A COM port is recognized by the PC.

communication.method/procedure: Power on SIM800A, then connect USB_VBUS, USB_DP, USB_DN, and GND to the PC.
communication.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: The module enters USB download mode automatically when it detects USB_VBUS and can communicate with USB_DP and USB_DN.

power.method/procedure: Use AT+CBC to monitor the VBAT voltage.
The source describes constant software monitoring of VBAT and states the reported URCs/automatic-power-off behavior at the documented thresholds.
power.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: At VBAT ≤3.5V report “UNDER-VOLTAGE WARNNING”; at ≥4.3V report “OVER-VOLTAGE WARNNING”; below 3.4V report “UNDER-VOLTAGE POWER OFF” and power off; above 4.4V report “OVER-VOLTAGE POWER OFF” and power off. The source says this function is disabled by default.

environmental.method/procedure: The table gives contact-discharge and air-discharge characteristics at temperature 25°C and humidity 45%; it lists VBAT/GND, UART1_RXD/TXD, antenna port, SPKP/SPKN/MICP/MICN, and PWRKEY.

ambiguities.issue: Pinout graphic labels are not present in the text extraction. The 68-pad pinout above is transcribed from Table 4 rather than inferred from Figure 2.

Table 15 (SIM pin definition) text extraction reports SIM_VDD=18, SIM_DATA=15, SIM_CLK=16, SIM_RST=17, and SIM_DET=14, conflicting with Table 4 values SIM_VDD=30 through SIM_DET=34. No reconciliation is inferred; the complete pinout uses Table 4.
The GPRS-class statements are internally inconsistent in the supplied document: class 12 default/class 10 optional versus class 1–12 option. Both are reported without selecting one.

The Table 4 I/O column appears merged in the text extraction for the keypad block and is blank for GPIO10/GPIO11/GPIO12. Keypad entries preserve the visually merged “I/O”; GPIO direction_type is null rather than inferred.

Several circuit figures are diagrammatic and their component placement/net connectivity is only partially represented by text extraction. Circuit descriptions are limited to labels and adjacent prose that are recoverable from the supplied text.
